sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the above, the acceptance by the Jews during the time of Mordechai and Esther was a completion of the initial beginning at the Giving of the Torah, achieved specifically through the work of the lower beings in exile.

translations.translation: And based on the above, one can understand what is written, "And the Jews accepted that which they had begun to do,"
for although at the time of the Giving of the Torah the Jewish people were at the ultimate level
(and then everything was already given,
as above),
nevertheless, then it was only "they had begun to do,"
a mere beginning,
because this was only from Above downward.
And afterward, in the service during the time of exile,
in the time of Mordechai and Esther,
when the strength of exile is in doubled and redoubled darkness
(as it was literally),
then the service is from the side of the lower beings,
"and the Jews accepted,"
which was not the case at the time of the Giving of the Torah.
And furthermore,
in the service during the time of exile there is an advantage over the time of the Giving of the Torah,
for specifically then the fulfillment of the Torah that they received at the Giving of the Torah, which was only in the aspect of "they had begun to do," is achieved,
because specifically during the time of exile
[in its simple sense,
and also in the subtlety of the matters,
when one contemplates
(in the manner mentioned above)
that even after all the matters he has effected through his service,
even when they are at the ultimate perfection,
nevertheless he is still in a state of exile
(spiritually),
because since the Holy One, blessed be He, assists him
he has the ability to reach an even higher level, to an incomparable degree,
in the manner of the expression of our Sages, of blessed memory,
("You toiled")
"and found," for the finding is beyond proportion to his toil and effort]
then each person is broken and crushed,
then they reach the light itself.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This connects to the weekly portion and the concept of "chen" (grace), which is an arousal from Above that follows the arousal from below, drawing from the Essence of the Ein Sof.

translations.translation: And one should connect what was stated above about the greatness of the advantage of the service of the lower beings,
that specifically through it the fulfillment of what they began to do is achieved,
with the weekly portion
[and in this itself, with the lesson of today, the third day
[whose concept is that "it is good" was doubled in it,
good for the heavens and good for the creations]
— according to the enactment of my master, father-in-law, the Rebbe, to learn each day of the week one portion of the weekly portion]
based on what is explained in the maamarim
and particularly in the maamar of my master, the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, from sixty years ago,
on our portion, on the verse,
"And now, if I have found grace in Your eyes... so that I may find grace in Your eyes... for I have found grace in Your eyes... for you have found grace in My eyes"
[for through this it will be, "and we shall be distinguished, I and Your people, from every nation on the face of the earth"
(and "we shall be distinguished" is like the concept of "wondrous" mentioned above)]
that one must understand what is the advantage of the matter of grace that Moshe Rabbeinu requested and pleaded so much for, to the point that this was the ultimate perfection of his request,
and through grace there will then be "and we shall be distinguished, I and Your people,"
for is it not written,
"Grace is false,"
and this is because grace is an aspect of an arousal from Above by itself,
and there is a great advantage in that which comes through an arousal from below.

And it is explained there about this, that there is an aspect of an arousal from Above that is drawn after the arousal from below, which is a drawing from the aspect of the Essence of the Ein Sof, which the arousal from below does not reach at all, and it is only in the aspect of a gift
(and this is called a free gift, which is the language of grace, etc.)
only that this is drawn after the perfection of the arousal from below,
like regarding a gift, our Sages, of blessed memory, said,
"Were it not that he had satisfaction for himself, etc.," even though it is in the aspect of a gift.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The service of Israel through faith in the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin (transcendent light) draws an arousal from Above that is beyond the order of Hishtalshelus, reaching the aspect of Kesser and Atzmus.

translations.translation: And the service in this is
[as understood from what is explained in the maamar there],
that there is

the matter of faith in the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin (immanent light), but in this aspect it is possible that there is something similar among the righteous of the nations of the world, and even among Israel it is possible that the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin is in the aspect of knowledge.
And the main faith of the souls of Israel is in the level of Sovev Kol Almin,
for this faith is only relevant to Israel,
for this is what is written,

"Hear, O Israel, the L-rd our G-d, the L-rd is One," which is the concept of acceptance and faith in the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin, and about this it is said "Hear, O Israel" specifically, for this faith is only in the souls of Israel
[in contrast to what is said, "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever," which applies to the contemplation of the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin].
And this is also what is stated in the Zohar,
that the ayin of "Shema" and the dalet of "Echad" are large letters, and through their combination the word "eid" (witness) is formed,
and it is explained in many places
that regarding something revealed there is no need and it is not applicable to have testimony,
and even regarding a matter that is destined to be revealed, the Torah does not require testimony,
but only specifically regarding something completely hidden,
the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin.
And this is what is written, "Hear, O Israel, the L-rd is One,"
which applies to each and every one of Israel, for they specifically are the witnesses who testify
that the L-rd is One
[to the point that in every situation and state that may be in his service, each and every one of Israel says "Hear, O Israel,"
as explained in the talks of my master, father-in-law, the Rebbe],
for the chet and dalet of "Echad" allude to the seven firmaments and the earth and the four directions of the world, and the alef alludes to the Alufo shel Olam (Master of the World),
and Israel, through their service, effect that He is One,
meaning that they draw into the world
(the chet and dalet)
the Alufo shel Olam
(the alef),
until they become unified in the pattern of the word "Echad," where the alef is the first letter together with the chet and dalet
(and the content of the word itself is the concept of unity),
and in such a manner that the alef of the Alufo shel Olam is the head
and the beginning of the word.
And behold, through this arousal from below of the service of Israel in the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin
("the L-rd is One"),

they draw an arousal from Above proportionate to the arousal from below, and afterward an arousal from Above that is above the aspect of the arousal from Above that comes through the arousal from below is drawn.
For the aspect of the arousal from Above drawn through the arousal from below is an aspect commensurate with the order of Hishtalshelus,
and one could say that this also applies to what is written,
"Behold, My angel will go before you,"
but Moshe's request was for the drawing of the aspect of the arousal from Above that is above this, by itself,
"And now, if I have found grace in Your eyes,"
the concept of grace,
until it would be "and we shall be distinguished, I and Your people,"
which applies
(in the Sefiros)
to the Sefirah of Kesser,
the innerness of Kesser, and to His very Essence, may He be blessed.
For although this aspect of the arousal from Above is drawn by itself, meaning that the arousal from below does not reach there,
nevertheless, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not dwell except in a place that is complete,

for there must first be the service of the lower beings in an arousal from below and the drawing of the arousal from Above proportionate to the arousal from below, and then, in the complete place, He dwells, as explained in Likkutei Torah on Shir HaShirim.
